comments.author: @atticus-rex
comments.text: I'm an A/V technician, please hear me out.  I really want to listen to your whole video. I've come here dozens of times but leave after about 3-5 mins.  I'd like to give you my professional advice; lower the bass and raise your conversational EQ to the higher ranges because I honestly can't stay focused on what you're saying. People without much inflection in their voices (monotone) do a massive disservice to themselves by raising the bass to higher levels over the mid range and higher ranges. This makes it difficult for people's brains to remain engaged and they lose interest. It's difficult to easily hear you as your voice is way too muffled, sounds like you're in the next room with a wall between. When the ear hears monotone and worse, low level monotone, it has to strain to hear, thus the brain cannot stay focused on the target sound, so it treats it as background noise. Your cadence and high bass level don't work together. People with flatter cadence need to be in high ranges to compensate. You're doing the exact opposite of what you should be doing. And to be clear, I don't have this issue with any other videos. Howard Stern for example uses high bass, but his cadence and inflections are energetic, so it works for him. Trust me, lower you bass, and raise the mid-range eq a little more, and raise the higher levels a lot more, you'll have better engagement. I hope you try it out because I would really love to stick around and learn from you. This was meant as constructive criticism from an Audio/Video engineer tech. Peace
